chunks: That which the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me: he said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS):
He said: I asked him about a man when he intends to perform istinja' — with which does he begin: the anus (maq'ada) or the urethra (ihlil)? He said: [Begin with] the anus, then the urethra.

Then he — may Allah the Exalted support him — said: When one has finished the istinja', let him stand and wipe his right hand over his belly, and let him say — and he mentioned the two supplications: the first has already been reported in a prior narration, and the second [is as follows].

key_terms.الدُّعَائَيْنِ: the two du'as — specific supplications prescribed as a sunnah act upon completing istinja'
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءِ: istinja' — ritual cleansing of the private parts (anus and urethra) immediately after relieving oneself; a prerequisite for valid taharah
key_terms.الْإِحْلِيلِ: ihlil — the urethral opening; point of exit for urine
key_terms.الْمَقْعَدَةِ: maq'ada — the anus/rectum; point of exit for solid waste

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, which body part should be cleansed first during istinja' — the anus or the urethra?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted by his companion 'Ammar al-Sabati, addresses the correct sequence for istinja' (ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself): the Imam rules that one begins with the anus (maq'ada) and proceeds to the urethra (ihlil). Sheikh al-Mufid appends a supplementary directive — drawn from the same body of transmission — prescribing that upon completing istinja', one should stand, pass the right hand over the belly, and recite two specific supplications, the first of which was recorded in a prior narration.
